claims.proposition_evaluated: At its meeting of 2026-08-26, the Infrastructure Committee (a standing committee of Council, not Council itself) carried a motion reducing the time each approved public speaker could speak from the five-minute standing limit in section 38(1) of Council Procedures Bylaw 18155 (consolidated 2025-10-29) to a maximum of three minutes for that meeting, at a meeting for which 60 to 80 entries were listed as approved speakers on item 7.6 (IS03688, Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration Program Update). The reason for the motion, whether registrants were complainants, and where they came from were not tested.
claims.interpretation_notes: Verdict under the primary measure. (1) Standing limit: 5 minutes per approved speaker under s.38(1). I read this only from search-engine extracts of the City's consolidated PDF, because direct fetches failed (see limitations). (2) The cut: under item 1.4, moved by M. Janz, the committee adjusted 'the rules on time limits as set out in section 38 of Bylaw 18155' for the 2026-08-26 meeting so that 'each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of three minutes'. It carried 6 to 0. (3) Coverage: the wording covers every approved speaker on every item of the meeting, not only item 7.6. (4) Primary count N (item 7.6 Requests to Speak, item 2.3), entries by panel: P1 15, P2 15, P3 15, P4 15, P5 4. N = 64 (reviewer's sum: 15+15+15+15+4). The additional-speaker motion at 2.3 concerns item 7.4 only, so it adds nothing to N. 64 is inside 60-80, which gives Supported. ALTERNATIVES (reported as qualifications). Alternative band 50-90 with N=64: Supported. N-all (every item in the 2.3 motions): 7.1 = 5; 7.3 = 1; 7.4 = 8 + 1 additional = 9; 7.6 = 64; N-all = 79 (reviewer's sum). That is inside 60-80, at its top edge, and inside 50-90, so Supported under both bands. A person approved on more than one item would be counted more than once in N-all. The redacted text can't show whether that happened. N-spoke (item 7.6 presentation lists): P1 16, P2 16, P3 18, P4 2, with no Panel 5 presentation list. N-spoke = 52 (reviewer's sum: 16+16+18+2). That is BELOW the primary band of 60-80, which gives Partially supported: the cut is established but the count is outside the band. It is inside 50-90, which gives Supported. Because N-spoke under the primary band changes the row, the finding is DEFINITION-SENSITIVE. If the holder's '70 in the queue' means the people who actually spoke, the figure does not fall within 60-80. Two-thirds check (reviewer's calculation): the minutes list 6 members (E. Rutherford, A. Salvador, R. Clarke, M. Janz, Mayor A. Knack as a member under s.15(3) of Bylaw 18156, and A. Paquette). Two-thirds of all 6 members is 4. All 6 voted in favour, so the special-resolution threshold in s.2/s.4 was met. The motion cites s.38, not s.4.

supporting_evidence.finding: Under item 1.4 (Adoption of Agenda), the third motion was moved by M. Janz: the committee adjusted the s.38 time limits for the 2026-08-26 meeting so that each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of three minutes, and each member of Council has three minutes to ask questions and three minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion. In favour (6): E. Rutherford, A. Salvador, R. Clarke, M. Janz, A. Knack, A. Paquette. Carried 6 to 0. No one opposed. No seconder is recorded.

supporting_evidence.finding: Bylaw 18155 s.38(1), as shown in search-engine extracts of the City's consolidated PDF (headed 'consolidated on October 29, 2025'), reads: 'Each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of 5 minutes'. Under s.38(2), an individual authorized to speak for multiple persons also gets a maximum of 5 minutes. Under s.4, Council or a Standing Committee may waive or modify any part of the bylaw by special resolution. Under s.2, a special resolution is a vote where at least two-thirds of all members of a Standing Committee vote in favour. Bylaw 20226 (Council Processes Amendment), which replaced s.38, also sets 5 minutes per approved speaker.
supporting_evidence.source_title: City of Edmonton Bylaw 18155, Council Procedures Bylaw (consolidated October 29, 2025)
supporting_evidence.establishes: That the standing per-speaker limit was 5 minutes, and that a standing committee can modify it by a vote of two-thirds of all its members. Read only through search-index extracts of this URL; the PDF itself returned HTTP 502 on every direct fetch on 2026-10-02.

limitations: ESSENTIAL-SOURCE ACCESS: The Bylaw 18155 PDF (https://www.edmonton.ca/sites/default/files/public-files/assets/Bylaws/C18155.pdf) returned HTTP 502 on four direct fetches on 2026-10-02, and the edmonton.ca bylaw index and Clerk FAQ also returned 502. I read s.1, s.2, s.4 and s.38 only through search-engine extracts of that URL and of Bylaw 20226. I could not read the consolidation's own list of amendments, so I cannot confirm from it that no amendment after 2025-10-29 bears on s.38. Searches found no 2026 amendment. If the run treats an essential source read only through search extracts as inaccessible, the stop rule applies.

Search extracts disagree on the councillor speak-to-motion limit in s.38: Bylaw 20226 says 2 minutes, while an extract of the consolidation said 5 minutes. So I cannot say whether the motion's 'three minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion' for members of Council shortened or lengthened that particular limit. This does not affect the per-speaker finding.

The live minutes and agenda pages returned HTTP 403 on 2026-10-02. I relied on the carried text (YF-EV-0209/0210). I cannot confirm whether the live page carries any later correction to items 1.4, 2.3 or 7.6. The carried text shows none.

Because redacted entries are identical, every count is a hand count of '[member of the public]' lines in the carried text. Panel 3 of the presentations (18 entries) is the longest run of identical lines and the most exposed to miscount.

The item 7.6 Panel 4 presentation list has 2 entries, and the motion text begins immediately after them. There is no Panel 5 presentation list, although 2.3 approved 19 entries across Panels 4 and 5. From the carried text alone I cannot tell whether this reflects the record or a truncation in carrying. If the live page lists more Panel 4/5 presenters, N-spoke rises.

Request panels and presentation panels do not line up (for example, organizations approved in Panel 2 presented in Panel 1). With names withheld, entries cannot be matched across lists, so no count of approved speakers who did not present is given.

Qualification 9 (earlier meetings since 2025-10-29 that adjusted the s.38 limits): the eScribe portal blocked automated access (403), so I could not browse it. Web searches restricted to pub-edmonton.escribemeetings.com for s.38 three-minute motions in 2026 found none. Absence is bounded by those searches as of 2026-10-02 and is not evidence that none exist.
Qualification 8 (stated reason for the motion): none identified. I searched the carried minutes items 1.4/2.3/2.4/7.6, the CBC/Yahoo report and web searches. The minutes record no reason.

Qualification 7: the minutes record no speaker given more or less than the limit and no motion extending any speaker's time. Item 7.6 lists 5 speaker presentation attachments (Panel 3 x2, Panels 1, 2 and 4 x1 each). The agenda page attachment list has none. Titles are not reproduced.
Qualification 2: s.38(2) (authorized representatives) is not separately addressed. The motion's 'each approved speaker' wording reads as covering them too.
unknowns: Whether the live, approved minutes differ from the carried text in items 1.4, 2.3 or 7.6, especially the Panel 4/5 presentation lists.
Whether any amendment to s.38 took effect between 2025-10-29 and 2026-08-26, since I could not read the consolidation's own amendment list.
Why the motion was moved. This is not tested, and the minutes record no reason.
Whether other committees adjusted s.38 limits at meetings since 2025-10-29.

calculations_needed: N (item 7.6 approved) = 15+15+15+15+4 = 64; entries with an organization = 2+8+3+2+0 = 15 (reviewer's count).
N-all = 5 (7.1) + 1 (7.3) + 9 (7.4: 8 + 1 additional) + 64 (7.6) = 79; entries with an organization = 5+1+6+15 = 27 (reviewer's count).
N-spoke (item 7.6 presented) = 16+16+18+2 = 52; entries with an organization = 5+6+1+0 = 12 (reviewer's count).

Band rows: N=64 is Supported under 60-80 and under 50-90. N-all=79 is Supported under 60-80 and under 50-90. N-spoke=52 is Partially supported under 60-80 (below the band) and Supported under 50-90. The finding is definition-sensitive.
Two-thirds of all members: 6 members x 2/3 = 4 needed. 6 voted in favour, so the threshold was met (reviewer's calculation).
what_would_change_my_verdict: A readable consolidation, or an amendment in force on 2026-08-26, showing a standing limit other than 5 minutes would make the verdict Partially supported.
Live minutes showing a different item 2.3 list for 7.6 (fewer than 60 or more than 80 entries), or a later correction to the 1.4 time-limit motion.
Evidence that the carried text omits an additional-speaker motion on item 7.6 that would push N above 80.
claims.suggested_one_line: Yes. The Infrastructure Committee voted 6–0 to cut every public speaker's time from five minutes to three for the August 26, 2026 meeting, and it had approved 64 entries to speak on the bike-lane item. Only 52 are recorded as having presented, so whether the claimed queue of 'seventy' fits depends on how the queue is counted.
claims.suggested_short_answer: The committee's minutes record a motion under item 1.4, moved by M. Janz and carried 6–0, limiting each approved speaker to three minutes for the August 26, 2026 meeting. The procedures bylaw's standing limit is five minutes. The committee approved 64 entries to speak on the bike-lane item (79 across the whole meeting). 52 are recorded as presenting on it. The minutes give no reason for the cut and do not record which way anyone spoke. This finding says nothing about whether the speakers were complainants, where they came from, or whether three minutes was enough.
suggested_tldr: Standing rule: up to 5 minutes per approved speaker (Bylaw 18155, s.38).
On 2026-08-26 the Infrastructure Committee carried 6–0 a motion setting 3 minutes for every approved speaker at that meeting.
Approved on the bike-lane item: 64 entries in 5 panels. Whole meeting: 79. Recorded as presenting on the item: 52.
Counting only people who presented, the figure falls outside 60–80, so the 'seventy' part is definition-sensitive.
